record.paper_title: Open problems in the theory of non-uniform hyperbolicity
record.context_brief: Mixed-sign central exponents for u-measures on partially hyperbolic attractors
record.original_question: Let f be a C^2 diffeomorphism with a partially hyperbolic attractor Λ, and let μ be a u-measure whose central Lyapunov exponents are nonzero on a set of positive μ-measure, with some central exponents positive and some negative. Assume that for every x in Λ the global strongly unstable manifold W^u(x) is dense in Λ. Must μ be ergodic? Must μ be the unique SRB measure for f? Must f be stably ergodic?

evidence.quote: Problem 8.5. Let f be a C2 diffeomorphism with a partially hyperbolic attractor Λ and µ a u-measure with nonzero central exponents (of which some are positive and some are negative) on a set of positive measure. Assume that for every x ∈ Λ the global strongly unstable manifold Wu(x) is dense in Λ. Is µ ergodic? Is it a unique SRB measure for f? Is f stably ergodic?

artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open problem in surveys on non-uniform hyperbolicity. Related results are known when the central exponents have a single sign (mostly contracting or mostly expanding), and stable ergodicity/Bernoulli results exist under additional hypotheses, but in the genuinely mixed-sign case with the density-of-unstable-leaves assumption the questions of ergodicity, uniqueness of SRB, and stable ergodicity remain open in the literature reviewed.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in the theory of non-uniform hyperbolicity
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 8.5 asks whether such a u-measure must be ergodic, the unique SRB measure, and whether f is stably ergodic.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed as open.

status_evidence.title: Stable ergodicity for partially hyperbolic attractors with negative central exponents
status_evidence.snippet: Treats the case of negative central exponents (single sign) and obtains stable ergodicity; the mixed-sign case is not resolved.
status_evidence.claim: Known partial results cover the one-sign case, not the mixed case.
